claims.claim: Under a fed high-fat condition, ziprasidone—a lipophilic, poorly soluble drug—had absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 59–60%, showing that a challenging solubility/lipophilicity profile can still meet F≥20% when food enhances absorption.

Sertindole, another lipophilic, poorly soluble antipsychotic, had oral bioavailability of approximately 74–75% that was not significantly affected by food, further supporting adequate oral bioavailability for this type of physicochemical profile.

No L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F<20% for the query or a close analog; the unfavorable physicochemical prior is not an endpoint measurement and is insufficient to predict low bioavailability.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement is provided for the query molecule or an exact structural analog such as itraconazole.
The fed-state formulation, dose, and food composition are unspecified for the query; food effects can be formulation-dependent.
No matched oral-versus-IV exposure data are available for the query; transfer relies on physicochemically and condition-matched but not structurally identical drugs.
High molecular weight, high logD, and low predicted solubility remain uncertainties, but they are not affirmative evidence of F<20%.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F≥20%) under fed state: the fed-condition absolute-F records for ziprasidone (~59–60%) and the food-insensitive high-F records for sertindole (~74–75%) provide transferable direction evidence, and no affirmative low-F evidence exists; the unfavorable physicochemical prior alone is insufficient to predict low.
